recipes.title: Chicken tikka masala
recipes.description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, charred under the grill and simmered in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.
recipes.source: Tastebook

lines.note: boneless and skinless, cut into bite-sized pieces
depending on how hot you like it

steps: Mix the yoghurt, garam masala, turmeric, garlic, lemon juice and a good pinch of salt in a bowl. Stir in the chicken, cover and leave in the fridge for at least an hour.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the chicken on a lined tray, shaking off any extra marinade, and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and golden, then add the green chilli and ginger and cook for a minute more.
Stir in the garam masala, cumin, paprika and chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Stir in the cream and the grilled chicken and simmer for 5 minutes. Season to taste and scatter over the coriander to serve.

recipes.title: Oat and raisin cookies
recipes.description: Chewy cookies with crisp edges, made with porridge oats and plenty of raisins.
recipes.source: Tastebook
steps: Beat the butter and sugar with a hand mixer until pale and fluffy, then beat in the golden syrup.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon (if using) and salt, then the oats and raisins, until the dough comes together.
Cover the bowl and chill the dough for 30 minutes, so the cookies hold their shape in the oven.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two baking trays. Roll the dough into 16 balls and space them well apart on the trays, flattening each one slightly.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Leave on the trays for 5 minutes, then move to a rack to cool.

recipes.title: Spaghetti aglio e olio
recipes.description: Spaghetti tossed in olive oil with gently fried garlic and chilli: dinner from the store cupboard in 20 minutes.
recipes.source: Tastebook
steps: Cook the spaghetti in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for a minute less than the packet says. Keep a mugful of the cooking water before you drain it.

While the pasta cooks, warm the oil in a large frying pan over a low heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Don't let it brown, or it turns bitter.
Tip the drained spaghetti into the frying pan with a splash of the cooking water and toss for a minute until every strand is glossy, adding more water if it looks dry.
Toss through the parsley, season with salt and serve with the parmesan, if using.

recipes.title: Greek salad
recipes.description: Tomatoes, cucumber, olives and a whole slab of feta, dressed with olive oil and oregano.
recipes.source: Tastebook
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, pepper and olives in a wide bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and half the oregano with a little salt and pepper, then pour it over the vegetables and toss gently.
Lay the feta on top in one piece, sprinkle over the rest of the oregano and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Spanish tortilla
recipes.description: A thick potato and onion omelette, cooked slowly in olive oil and good warm or cold.
recipes.source: Tastebook
steps: Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning now and then, until soft but not browned.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl. Lift the potatoes and onion out of the pan with a slotted spoon, leaving the oil behind, and stir them into the eggs. Leave for 5 minutes.

Pour all but a tablespoon of the oil out of the pan (keep it for another day) and put the pan back over a medium heat. Tip in the egg mixture and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until set underneath but still a little loose on top.
Put a large plate over the pan and turn it over in one confident movement, then slide the tortilla back into the pan, cooked side up. Cook for 3 minutes more.
Slide the tortilla onto a board and leave it to rest for 10 minutes before cutting it into wedges.

recipes.title: Black bean chilli
recipes.description: A big pot of vegetarian chilli: dried black beans simmered with smoky chipotle and ancho chillies, cumin, oregano and tomatoes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 tablespoons (30 mL) corn oil or other vegetable oil
2 tablespoons (30 mL) wine vinegar (red or white)

steps: Put the beans in a large pot, cover with water by about 5 cm and leave to soak overnight. Drain, cover with fresh water, bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 2 hours.

Heat the oil in a very large pot over a medium-high heat. Fry the onion for about 3 minutes until tender, then add the garlic, chipotle and ancho chillies, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, cayenne and vinegar and fry for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, passata and the water. Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the beans with their cooking liquid and simmer for an hour.
Serve with or without soured cream.

recipes.title: Bread pudding
recipes.description: Torn bread and raisins soaked in a cinnamon and vanilla custard and baked until set, served cold or warm in squares.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: stale or fresh, with or without crusts
ingredient_lines.original_text: 6 slices of bread, with or without crusts. Slightly stale or new bread is acceptable.

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan).
Tear the bread into small pieces, or cut it into cubes, and put it in a 20 cm square baking dish, mixing in the raisins as you go.
Pour the melted butter over the bread.
In a bowl, lightly beat the eggs, then mix in the sugar, milk, cinnamon and vanilla.
Pour this over the bread, pressing the bread down lightly so that all of it is soaked.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Take out and leave to cool. Serve cold or warm, spooned out or cut into squares.

recipes.title: Huevos rancheros
recipes.description: Fried eggs on crisp-fried corn tortillas, covered in a quick ranchero sauce of tomatoes, onion and chilli.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 plum tomatoes, peeled, seeded and chopped
1 tablespoon cilantro or parsley (optional), finely chopped

steps: For the ranchero sauce, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic and fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Add the tomatoes, chillies, chilli powder, sugar, salt and a few grinds of black pepper and turn down to a simmer. Simmer for about 10 minutes, until the sauce starts to thicken.
Stir in the coriander, turn off the heat and cover the pan to keep the sauce warm.
In a second frying pan, lightly fry the tortillas in 1 tablespoon of the oil. Lift out and drain.
Add the rest of the oil to the second pan if needed and fry the eggs sunny side up. Put the eggs on the tortillas and spoon over the sauce.

recipes.title: Pot roast
recipes.description: A beef joint browned and then braised for hours in a low oven with wine, balsamic vinegar, herbs, carrots and potatoes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ea. (2 ½ pounds / 1.1 kg) bottom round roast

ingredient_lines.note: peeled and cut into 2 cm pieces
ingredient_lines.original_text: 3 carrots, peeled and cut into ¾-inch (2 cm) pieces

steps: Season the beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat half the olive oil in a 6-litre casserole dish over a medium-high heat. Add the beef and brown it on all sides.
Lift the beef onto a plate and keep warm.
Add the rest of the oil and the carrots, onion and potatoes to the dish. Cook until the onion is lightly browned at the edges.
Lift out the vegetables and keep warm.
Deglaze the dish with the stock, then stir in the garlic, wine, tomato juice, rosemary, thyme, oregano, balsamic vinegar and flour. Turn the heat down to low and return the vegetables and beef.
Cover and cook in the oven at 110°C (90°C fan) for 6 hours.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Skillet cornbread
recipes.description: A golden, crusty cornbread from the American South, baked in a smoking-hot pan so the bottom crisps, and good beside a pot of beans.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ¼ cups yellow or white cornmeal
2–3 tbsp melted butter or pan drippings

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Grease an ovenproof frying pan, ideally cast iron, with a little bacon fat or oil. Butter is best avoided here, as it can burn while the pan heats.
Put the pan in the oven until the fat is smoking hot. This gives the cornbread a good crust underneath.
In a bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, mix them well, then stir in the polenta.
In a second bowl, beat the egg well, then beat in the melted butter and the milk until well mixed.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ones and mix with quick strokes, taking care not to overmix.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden brown and a knife pushed into the middle comes out clean.

recipes.title: Lancashire hotpot
recipes.description: Layers of lamb, onion and sliced potato with herbs, slowly baked in water until the meat is tender and the top potatoes are golden.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 lb (900 g) neck of lamb or mutton
1 large or 2 small white onions, diced

steps: Dice the lamb. Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Lay some of the potatoes over the bottom of a casserole dish and cover with a handful of the onion. Put a layer of lamb on top and sprinkle with herbs.
Repeat the layers until the dish is full, finishing with a layer of potatoes.
Pour in the boiling water until it reaches the top of the dish, adding more if needed.
Bake for at least an hour; mutton needs longer.

recipes.title: Rhubarb crumble
recipes.description: Sharp rhubarb baked under a crisp crumble of plain and wholemeal flour, butter and sugar, best served warm with custard.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: cut into pieces about 1.5 cm long
ingredient_lines.original_text: 400 g (1 ¾ cup or 14 oz) rhubarb, cut into pieces roughly 1.5 cm long (no need to be consistent)
75 g (2 ½ oz) butter or margarine, cut in pieces
50 g (1 ¾ oz) white granulated sugar

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Rinse and drain the rhubarb and put it in a deep ovenproof dish. Add the brown sugar and mix briefly.
Put both flours in a mixing bowl and add the butter. Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle over the granulated sugar and cinnamon and mix in briefly.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit in an even layer, without pressing it down.
Bake uncovered for 35 to 45 minutes, until crisp and lightly browned. Serve with custard.

recipes.title: Shortbread
recipes.description: Crumbly, buttery biscuits made from just flour, butter and sugar, cut into fingers and baked slowly until pale gold.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 380 g (1 ½ cup / 13 ½ oz) all-purpose flour
110 g (½ cup / 4 oz) white granulated sugar

steps: Heat the oven to 140°C (120°C fan).
Cream the butter with the sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift in the flour and salt and work them into the butter and sugar until fully combined.
Shape the dough into a ball and roll it out about 1.3 cm thick. If it is hard to handle, chill it for 10 to 15 minutes first.
Cut into squares or fingers, put them on a baking tray and prick the tops with a fork in two lines.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until lightly browned.
Leave to cool on a wire rack, then keep in an airtight tin in a cool place.

recipes.title: Steak and ale pie
recipes.description: Chunks of stewing steak slowly simmered in ale and stock with herbs and mustard, then baked under a lid of puff pastry.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 900 g (2 lb) good beef stewing steak, at room temperature

ingredient_lines.note: a handful of the three herbs together
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 handful fresh thyme, marjoram and chopped parsley

ingredient_lines.note: a handful of the three herbs together
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 handful fresh thyme, marjoram and chopped parsley

ingredient_lines.note: chopped, a handful of the three herbs together
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 handful fresh thyme, marjoram and chopped parsley

steps: Cut the beef into cubes of about 2.5 cm.
Heat a little oil in a saucepan and fry the onion gently without letting it colour.
Add the beef and cook until it is browned all over.
Stir in the flour and cook for about a minute until it turns dark brown.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, marjoram, mustard, bay leaf and some salt and pepper.
Slowly pour in the stock and ale, then bring to the boil.
Simmer gently for about 1½ hours, until the beef is almost tender.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Take the pan off the heat, skim off any fat, check the seasoning and stir in the parsley.
Spoon the filling into a pie dish, or individual dishes, cover with the pastry and trim the edges.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the pastry is well risen and golden brown.

recipes.title: Toad in the hole
recipes.description: Sausages roasted in a hot tin, then baked in a Yorkshire pudding batter until it puffs up crisp and golden around them.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Make the batter: sift the flour into a bowl and beat in the eggs until smooth. Add the milk a little at a time, beating as you go, then season with the salt and pepper.
Put the sausages and oil in a roasting tin and bake for 10 minutes, so the sausages start to cook and the tin gets very hot.
Pour the batter into the hot tin around the sausages; the oil should sizzle as it goes in.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes without opening the oven door, until the batter has risen and is browned and crisp outside and firm inside. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Welsh rarebit
recipes.description: Toast covered in a rich, smooth sauce of cheddar melted into beer and cream, sharpened with mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

ingredient_lines.note: dark, such as porter or stout
ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 fl oz (60 ml) beer such as porter (Guinness will do)

steps: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a low heat and whisk in the flour.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, whisking all the time and taking care not to let the flour brown.
Whisk in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper until smooth.
Add the beer and whisk to combine.
Pour in the cream and whisk until smooth.
Add the cheese a little at a time, stirring constantly, until it has melted and the sauce is smooth; this takes 4 to 5 minutes.
Pour over the toast and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Arroz con pollo
recipes.description: Browned chicken pieces simmered with saffron rice, peppers, tomatoes and coriander in chicken stock, finished with peas.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ea. (1.3–1.8 kg) chicken, cut into serving pieces

ingredient_lines.note: enough to cover the base of the pan
threads, or 1 tsp yellow food colouring
ingredient_lines.original_text: 8 saffron threads or 1 teaspoon food coloring for yellow rice
370 g (2 cups) medium or long-grain rice

steps: Season the chicken with two pinches of salt and a pinch of pepper.
Pour just enough olive oil into a large frying pan to cover the base and heat it.
Fry the chicken until browned all over. Either lift it out and set it aside, or leave it in the pan.
Fry the garlic until golden, taking care as it burns easily.
Add the onion, red pepper, tomatoes and paprika and fry until the vegetables are tender.
Tip everything into a large stewing pot.
Add the coriander, stock and saffron (or food colouring) and bring to a rolling boil.
Stir in the rice. Simmer over a medium heat until the rice is cooked and the liquid absorbed, adding more stock or water if it dries out before the rice is done.
If you took the chicken out, return it to the pot and cover it with the rice. Leave for 2 to 3 minutes to warm through.
Scatter the peas over the rice and serve.

recipes.title: Rice with black beans
recipes.description: Cuban black beans slow-cooked with a garlicky pepper and onion sofrito, a splash of vinegar and wine, served over fluffy rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: large, halved, seeds and stem removed
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 large green pepper, cut in half with seeds and stem removed
4 cloves of garlic, smashed and chopped

ingredient_lines.note: large, seeds and stem removed, chopped
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 large green pepper, seeds and stem removed, then chopped

ingredient_lines.note: or ½ sachet of low-calorie sweetener
ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 tbsp sugar (or ½ packet of low-calorie sweetener)
2 tbsp dry white wine (cooking wine or dry sherry is fine)

ingredient_lines.note: for the beans and the rice

steps: The night before, wash the beans and leave them to soak in a large pot with 2.4 litres of water and the halved green pepper.
The next day, cook the beans in the same water at a gentle boil, stirring now and then, for about an hour, until softer.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a frying pan and fry the onion, garlic and chopped green pepper until soft, 5 to 10 minutes. This is the sofrito.

Ladle about 240 ml of the beans with some of their liquid into a blender and blend until smooth. Stir this into the sofrito, then tip the contents of the frying pan into the pot of beans. Add the salt, pepper, oregano, bay leaf and sugar.
Boil gently for about another hour, stirring now and then. Add the vinegar and wine.
Boil for about another hour to thicken, then stir in 2 tablespoons of olive oil.
Meanwhile, put the rice, 1.1 litres of water and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in another large saucepan.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Once the water has been absorbed, fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the beans over the rice, or in bowls beside it.

recipes.title: Ropa vieja
recipes.description: Cuban shredded beef, pressure-cooked then simmered with peppers, onion, garlic, tomato and red wine.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or another cut with long threads
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 kg boiled beef (preferably flank steak, but any meat with long threads will do)
1 cup red cooking wine or beer

steps: Cut the beef into medium pieces. Cover with water in a pressure cooker, add a teaspoon of the olive oil to stop it foaming and a teaspoon of salt, and cook for about 15 minutes. Keep 240 ml of the cooking liquid.
Shred the beef into thin strips with a fork. Chop the onion, slice the peppers into thin strips and finely chop the garlic.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large pan and fry the garlic and onion briefly, then add the peppers and fry a little longer. Add the beef, passata, salt, bay leaf, wine and the kept cooking liquid.
Cook over a low heat for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring a few times. Season to taste.

recipes.title: Chow mein
recipes.description: A vegetarian chow mein of crisp-fried noodles topped with stir-fried seitan, pak choi, mushrooms and peppers in a glossy soy sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Vegetable oil for frying, as needed

lines.original_text: ¼ cup water or low-sodium vegetable broth

steps: An hour or two before cooking, rinse the bean sprouts and leave them to drain thoroughly.
Cut the seitan into thin strips. Mix it with the shiitake, sesame oil, soy sauce, salt and pepper, then the cornflour, and leave to marinate for 20 to 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the sauce: dissolve the cornflour in the 4 tbsp of water in a small bowl, then whisk in the stock, soy sauce, salt and pepper. Set aside.
Soften the noodles in a pan of boiling salted water, then plunge them into cold water and drain thoroughly.

Cut the celery and pak choi into 1 cm pieces on the diagonal (if using broccoli, peel the stalks and slice thinly). Slice the mushrooms, cut the pepper into chunks, chop the red onion and slice the spring onion.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over a high heat and add 2 tbsp of oil. Fry the noodles in batches until golden, then lift out onto a serving plate.
Heat 2 tbsp more oil and add the red onion and the seitan, keeping any leftover marinade. Let the seitan brown, then stir-fry until nearly cooked through. Lift out.

Stir-fry the bean sprouts, celery, pak choi, mushrooms and pepper one at a time, seasoning each with a little salt and adding oil as needed, and lift each out when done. Add 60 ml of water to the pak choi or broccoli and cover while it cooks.

Stir the sauce again. Return everything to the wok, push it to the sides and pour the sauce and any leftover marinade into the middle, stirring quickly until it thickens. Toss everything together with the spring onion.
Spoon the vegetables and sauce over the noodles, scatter with the toasted sesame seeds and serve hot.

recipes.title: Hongshao rou
recipes.description: Shanghai-style red braised pork belly: cubes of pork caramelised in sugar, then simmered with soy, rice wine and star anise into a sticky, dark glaze.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oil and sugar together in a medium saucepan over a high heat until the sugar melts and turns brown.
Add the pork and brown it all over.
Lower the heat and add the stock, ginger, star anise, soy sauce and rice wine.
Cover tightly and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch on the bottom.
Take off the lid and add most of the spring onions, keeping a few back to garnish.
Boil until only a thick, dark gravy is left.
Serve with rice, scattered with the rest of the spring onions. If you can, chill it for a day first so the flavours develop, then reheat.

recipes.title: Mapo tofu
recipes.description: Soft silken tofu and minced beef simmered in a fiery, numbing Sichuan sauce of chilli bean paste and Sichuan pepper.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 small piece of ginger, minced (about 2 tsp)
200 g (7 oz) minced beef, or pork
1 tbsp Szechuan pepper, roasted and ground
3–4 green onions, cut into 2 cm (1 inch) pieces

steps: If using dried mushrooms, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes while you prepare everything else, then slice them.
Fry the onion with the ginger and chilli flakes in a pan over a medium heat until soft.
Add the mince and garlic and fry until browned.
Stir in the tofu, chilli bean paste, Sichuan pepper, soy sauce, rice wine, spring onions and mushrooms. Lower the heat and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Chocolate mousse
recipes.description: A light, airy French mousse of melted dark chocolate folded with whisked egg whites and whipped cream, chilled until set.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 200 g (8 oz) bittersweet chocolate, chopped (see notes)

steps: Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water.
Separate the eggs.
Whisk the egg whites and the cream separately until very firm, and put both in the fridge.
Put the egg yolks and hot water (hot tap water, 50–60°C, is enough) in a mixing bowl. Beat slowly with a hand mixer while adding the sugar, then speed up until the mixture is thick and pale yellow.
Once the chocolate has cooled enough to touch, stir it into the yolk mixture straight away, so it doesn't cook the yolks.
With a whisk, not the mixer, fold in the egg whites in three parts, then the whipped cream.
While the mousse is still loose, divide it between serving dishes. Chill for 4 to 6 hours, until firm.

recipes.title: Coq au vin
recipes.description: Chicken braised slowly in red wine with mushrooms, carrot, onion, garlic and herbs, a French classic.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: jointed, or drumsticks, thighs and breasts
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1.5 kg (about 3.5 lbs) chicken, jointed (or drumsticks, thighs, breasts); get the giblets, and the blood if you can; season beforehand; marrow is important.

steps: Mix the flour, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken, onion and carrot in the seasoned flour and set aside.
Heat a little oil in a wide frying pan and fry the mushrooms, then set them aside.
Brown the chicken pieces a few at a time in a little more oil, then set aside.
Brown the onion and carrot. Put the chicken in a large casserole over a medium-high heat with the onion, carrot, mushrooms and thyme.
Mix the wine, garlic and basil and pour it over the chicken.
Cover and cook, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and cooked through, 1 to 1½ hours.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup
recipes.description: Potage parmentier: leeks and floury potatoes simmered in salted water, puréed until silky and finished with a little cream.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 3–4 cups (~1 lb / 450 g) sliced leeks or onions

ingredient_lines.note: floury, such as Maris Piper, peeled and thickly sliced
ingredient_lines.original_text: 3–4 cups (700–900 g / 2 lb) floury potatoes (e.g. Idaho, Maris Piper), peeled and thickly sliced

ingredient_lines.note: table salt, or 1 tbsp sea salt
ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 tbsp table salt or 1 tbsp sea/rock salt
White pepper, freshly ground, to taste

ingredient_lines.note: up to 450 g, thinly sliced, such as broccoli stems or asparagus stalks
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1–2 cups (up to 450 g / 1 lb) vegetables (optional), thinly sliced
1–2 handfuls flat-leaf parsley or watercress (optional), rough chopped

steps: If using leeks, cut off the roots and dark green leaves, then wash them very thoroughly to remove all the grit.

Put the leeks, potatoes, any other vegetables or herbs, the water and salt in a large pot and bring to the boil. Lower the heat and simmer gently, partly covered, for 45 to 50 minutes, until the vegetables mash easily against the side of the pot.
Purée the soup through a food mill with a fine disc, or pulse it in a blender just until smooth and pass it through a fine sieve.
Chill the soup to serve cold, or reheat it gently to a simmer. Keep any leftovers covered in the fridge.
Stir 1½ to 2 teaspoons of cream into each bowl just before serving. Taste and season with salt and white pepper.

recipes.title: Potatoes Anna
recipes.description: Thinly sliced potatoes layered with plenty of melted butter and baked into a crisp, golden French potato cake.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan).
Melt the butter in a small pan.
Slice the potatoes thinly and press the slices between kitchen paper to dry them.
Brush a 23 cm round pie tin with melted butter. Layer the potato slices in the tin, brushing each layer with butter and finishing with butter on top.
Cover and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for a further 30 minutes, until golden.

recipes.title: Spaetzle
recipes.description: Little Swabian egg noodles made from a soft batter pressed or grated straight into boiling salted water, to serve with meat and sauce or with cheese and onions.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Mix the flour, eggs, salt and most of the water together by hand or with an electric mixer.
Add just enough of the rest of the water to make a dough that is slightly sticky but still elastic and stiff.
Beat the dough until bubbles rise in it.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.

If using a board, spread a spoonful of dough on a wooden board and scrape thin strips of it into the boiling water with a knife or the edge of a grater. If using a spaetzle maker or press, put a spoonful of dough in it and press it through the holes into the water. The spaetzle are done when they rise and float on the surface.
Lift the spaetzle out with a slotted spoon into a lightly oiled bowl, and carry on with the rest of the dough.

recipes.title: Pastitsio
recipes.description: A Greek baked pasta of macaroni bound with egg and parmesan, topped with cinnamon-scented meat sauce and a thick, golden béchamel.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 250 g macaroni pasta (or Greek pastitsio noodles)
¾ cup grated fresh Parmesan or Feta cheese

steps: For the meat sauce, heat the oil in a large pan and soften the onions until translucent.
Add the mince and cook until well browned.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, then the tomato purée, water, wine, stock powder and cinnamon. Simmer uncovered until thick.
Tip into a bowl and leave to cool, then stir in the egg.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a pan. Stir in the flour and cook, stirring, until bubbling.
Take the pan off the heat and gradually add the milk; it will thicken and then thin again.
Return to the heat and cook until the sauce bubbles and thickens. Stir in the parmesan until melted and smooth.
Tip into a bowl, cool slightly, then mix in the egg yolks.
For the pasta, boil the macaroni as the packet says until tender. Drain, tip into a bowl and mix the hot pasta with the parmesan and eggs.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 2.5-litre baking dish.
Press the pasta into the base of the dish, spread the meat sauce on top, then pour over the béchamel and smooth it. Scatter over the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 1 hour until golden brown, then leave to rest for at least 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Spanakopita
recipes.description: Greek spinach pie: a filling of spinach, herbs, feta and cottage cheese baked between buttery layers of crisp filo.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or 580 g frozen spinach, thawed and drained
ingredient_lines.original_text: 900 g (2 lbs) fresh spinach or 580 g (20 oz) frozen, thawed, and drained spinach
¾ cup small curd cottage cheese
¼ cup freshly grated parmesan cheese

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Wash the spinach, remove any large stalks and chop. Steam it over boiling water for 2 minutes, until wilted, then drain, pressing out the liquid with the back of a spoon.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and cook the onion until just soft. Add the spring onions and cook until limp. Take off the heat and stir in the parsley, dill, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Add the feta, cottage cheese, parmesan, spinach and lemon juice to the pan and mix. Add the eggs and mix again gently.

Brush a 23 × 30 cm baking dish with some of the melted ghee. Lay a sheet of filo over the base, letting the edges come up the sides, and brush with ghee. Keep layering and brushing until the base is covered with about 8 sheets.
Spread half the filling over the filo with a spatula.
Cover with 5 to 8 more sheets, brushing each with ghee. Spread the rest of the filling on top.
Cover with 5 to 8 more sheets, brushing each as before. Roll in the overhanging edges, crumble any broken pieces over the top and drizzle with the rest of the ghee.
Bake on a middle shelf for 45 minutes, until puffed and golden. Leave to rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

recipes.title: Aloo gobi
recipes.description: Potatoes and cauliflower cooked in ghee with cumin, turmeric and tomatoes until soft, finished with garam masala, mint and lemon.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 800 g (6.5 ea.) medium tomatoes, diced or puréed
4–5 potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes
3–5 tablespoons of ghee or vegetable oil

steps: Heat the ghee or oil in a large frying pan, wok or karahi.
Add the cumin seeds and cook until they turn light brown.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander, chilli powder and salt, then the tomatoes.
When the mixture turns glossy with oil, add the cauliflower and potatoes.
Cook, stirring now and then, until the cauliflower and potatoes are soft.
Stir in the garam masala, the mint leaves and the lemon juice.

recipes.title: Chana masala
recipes.description: A Punjabi chickpea curry of onions, tomatoes and toasted whole spices, simmered until thick and eaten with rice, puri or naan.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
recipes.photo_author: Simon Law (sfllaw) from Montréal, QC, Canada
steps: Wash the chickpeas, then leave them to soak overnight in plenty of water, with a few centimetres of water above them, as they swell a lot.

The next day, drain the chickpeas and put them in a large pan with the 500 ml of fresh water and salt to taste. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 60 to 90 minutes until tender (or cook for 10 minutes at high pressure in a pressure cooker).

Heat the oil in a heavy-based pan. Add the coriander, cumin and nigella seeds and cook briefly until they crackle. Quickly add the onion and garlic, lower the heat to medium and fry until the onion is translucent.
Add the garam masala, tomatoes, turmeric and a little salt and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked chickpeas, lower the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Spoon into a serving bowl, scatter over the coriander and serve with rice or bread.

recipes.title: Chicken biryani
recipes.description: Spiced, yoghurt-marinated chicken and golden onions layered with basmati rice, topped with saffron and baked slowly until tender.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 3 cloves of garlic, crushed and chopped

steps: Cook the soaked, washed rice in plenty of boiling water until just tender, then drain.
In a bowl, mix the chicken with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic, salt, turmeric, cumin, cloves, chillies and puréed tomatoes, and leave to marinate.

Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Heat the oil in a pan, add the cinnamon stick, peppercorns and cardamom pods for a few seconds, then add the onions and fry until golden brown. Stir them into the chicken.
Grease a deep, wide, heavy-based ovenproof pan. Spread in a layer of rice, add the chicken mixture, top with the rest of the rice and scatter the saffron over.
Cover and bake for 1 to 1½ hours, until the chicken is cooked through: cut into a piece to check.
Serve the biryani with yoghurt on the side.

recipes.title: Kheer
recipes.description: A thick Indian rice pudding simmered in milk with sultanas and cardamom, finished with almonds and a splash of rose water.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 250 ml (1 cup) long grain white rice

steps: Bring the milk to the boil, stirring often so it doesn't catch on the bottom of the pan.
Add the rice and simmer gently, stirring, until thick (about 20 minutes).
Stir in the sugar, sultanas and ground cardamom seeds and cook for 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the almonds and rose water, and cover until ready to serve.

recipes.title: Naan
recipes.description: Soft, puffy flatbreads made from a simple yoghurt dough, baked in a very hot oven and brushed with butter while warm.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Knead the flour, yoghurt, bicarbonate of soda and salt together with enough of the water to make a soft dough; you may not need all of it.
Wrap the dough in a damp muslin cloth and leave it to rise for 2 to 3 hours.
Heat the oven as hot as it will go. Divide the dough into small balls.
Roll the balls out into ovals or rounds with a rolling pin, or slap and stretch them with your hands.
Brush the tops with water and bake on a hot baking tray.
The naans should puff up a little and be ready in 4 to 5 minutes.
Brush the naans with butter and serve hot.

recipes.title: Pasta e fagioli
recipes.description: A thick Italian stew of white beans simmered slowly in olive oil with garlic and bay, then stirred through with small macaroni and chilli.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 teaspoon or more crushed or ground hot red pepper
½ pound small diameter macaroni (whole wheat is best)

steps: Put the washed beans in a large pot with three times their volume of salted water.
Soak overnight, or bring to the boil, boil for 2 minutes, then cover and leave to stand for an hour.
Bring the beans to the boil in their soaking water, without draining.
Skim off the foam and add the oil, garlic and bay leaf.
Simmer for about 2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Cook the macaroni in boiling water for 6 to 7 minutes, so it is still firm.
Drain the macaroni, keeping some of the cooking water.
Stir the macaroni and chilli flakes into the beans and simmer until the pasta is al dente, adding a little of the kept water if needed.
Season with salt, and garnish with more chilli to taste and the parsley.

recipes.title: Spaghetti alla puttanesca
recipes.description: Spaghetti in a punchy tomato sauce with anchovies, garlic, black olives, capers and a little dried chilli.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: unsalted, crushed into a paste; leave out for the Neapolitan version
ingredient_lines.original_text: 115 grams (4 ounces) unsalted anchovy fillets, crushed into a paste (omit anchovies for Neapolitan version)
200 grams (7 ounces) black olives, pitted and chopped

ingredient_lines.note: salted, rinsed well and roughly chopped
ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 tablespoons salted capers, washed well and coarsely chopped
900 grams (roughly 2 pounds) plum tomatoes, peeled and puréed

steps: Put the olive oil, garlic and anchovy paste in a frying pan over a medium heat.
Before the garlic browns, add the olives, capers, puréed tomatoes and chillies.
Add 2 or 3 pinches of salt and stir over a high heat, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water (at least 4 litres for every 450 g) until al dente, then drain.
Put the spaghetti in a large serving bowl, coat it with the sauce and scatter over the parsley.
Toss and serve hot.

recipes.title: Tiramisù
recipes.description: Coffee-soaked sponge fingers layered with a light mascarpone cream and finished with a dusting of cocoa.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 400 g of lady fingers (savoiardi) (or sponge cake)

steps: Make the espresso and leave it to cool a little.
Separate two of the eggs, putting the yolks in one bowl and the whites in another. Add the two extra whites to the whites.
Beat the sugar into the egg yolks, then beat in the mascarpone until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites until they hold stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture.
Quickly dip both sides of each sponge finger in the espresso. Layer the soaked fingers and the mascarpone cream in a large dish, starting with fingers and finishing with cream.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours. Dust the top with cocoa powder just before serving.

recipes.title: Niku jaga
recipes.description: A homely Japanese stew of thinly sliced beef, potatoes and onion simmered in a sweet soy and mirin broth with shirataki noodles.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Cut the potatoes into bite-sized pieces and leave them to soak in cold water.
Put the mirin, soy sauce, sugar, ginger and beef in a saucepan and boil gently for 2 to 3 minutes.
Lift out the beef. Add the drained potatoes, onion and water to the pan and bring to the boil.
Simmer uncovered until the broth has reduced to about a third.
Return the beef to the pan, add the shirataki noodles and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Okonomiyaki
recipes.description: Japanese savoury pancakes of cabbage and spring onion in a light batter, topped with bacon and finished with okonomiyaki sauce, bonito flakes and nori.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: or yam flour if you can get it
lines.original_text: 1 cup all-purpose flour (or yam flour if you can get it)
¾ cup finely sliced cabbage (about 2 inches long by ¼ inch wide)

lines.note: white and freshest green parts, cut into 1 cm rounds
lines.original_text: 2–3 green onions, chopped into ¼" rounds (use white part and freshest bit of green part)
¼ cup mozzarella cheese (optional; other cheese may be substituted)

lines.note: small, or thinly sliced chicken or beef
lines.original_text: 10 small slices of chicken, bacon or beef (your choice)

steps: Mix the flour, water and eggs until smooth, 25 to 30 strokes with a spoon or whisk; don't overmix.
Gently fold in the cabbage, spring onions and cheese.
Heat a griddle or non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. When it's hot, add the oil.
Add about 80 ml of batter and flatten it slightly. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
When the underside is golden brown, lay the bacon on top and press it in slightly. Turn the pancake and fry for 5 minutes, until golden on the other side.
Turn once more and fry topping side up for another minute. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve topped with okonomiyaki sauce, nori and bonito flakes.

recipes.title: Bibimbap
recipes.description: Korean rice bowls topped with sesame-dressed carrots, spinach and bean sprouts, soy-fried beef and a fried egg, with gochujang and kimchi on the side.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 8 oz bean sprouts, with beans attached
¾–1 ½ cup white rice, steamed

steps: Cut the carrots into matchsticks. Boil them in a covered pan of salted water for a few minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool. Drain again, put in a bowl and toss with the sesame oil, ground sesame seeds, garlic and salt.
Put the spinach in a large covered pan with 3 cm of water. Bring to the boil and cook, stirring now and then, until dark green and much reduced.
Drain the spinach, cool it under cold water and squeeze out the water with your hands. Cut into 3 cm pieces and mix in a bowl with its sesame oil, sesame seeds and garlic.
Blanch the bean sprouts in a pan of salted water until they turn translucent. Drain, tip into a bowl and toss with their sesame oil, sesame seeds, garlic and salt.
Slice the steak thinly, but not paper-thin. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and, when it's hot but not smoking, stir-fry the beef.
While the beef cooks, add its sesame oil, sesame seeds and garlic, and cook until well browned. Add the soy sauce and cook until the liquid has boiled off.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan and fry the eggs, flipping them briefly so the yolks stay runny.
Put the rice in bowls. Arrange the carrots, spinach, bean sprouts, beef and cucumber separately on top, with an egg in the middle.
Serve with the gochujang and kimchi in small bowls on the side. To eat, stir everything together.

recipes.title: Bulgogi
recipes.description: Korean barbecued beef: wafer-thin slices marinated in soy, sugar, sesame oil and garlic, then seared quickly over a fierce heat.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 lb (450 g) beef suitable for grilling, sliced as thin as possible
3 green onions, sliced on the bias

steps: Mix everything together in a large bowl and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge for the best flavour and tenderness.
Heat a griddle or large frying pan over a medium-high heat and sear the beef and vegetables in batches until browned.
Serve with rice, spooning the pan juices over it.

recipes.title: Cochinita pibil
recipes.description: Pork shoulder marinated overnight in annatto, citrus and spices, then slow-roasted in banana leaves until it falls apart, from the Yucatán.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Banana leaves and/or heavy-duty aluminium foil

ingredient_lines.note: cooked, or taco shells or tortillas, to serve
ingredient_lines.original_text: White or Spanish rice, taco shells, or tortillas for serving

steps: Grind the annatto seeds, cumin seeds, peppercorns, allspice and cloves to a fine powder in a spice grinder or a pestle and mortar.
Remove the seeds and white membranes from the habanero chillies and chop them roughly. Leave some of the seeds in if you want it hotter.
Blend the orange juice, vinegar, chillies, salt, garlic and the ground spices until smooth, then stir in the lemon juice and the tequila.
Cut the pork into 5 cm chunks, leaving the fat on to keep it moist as it roasts; you can trim it off after cooking if you like.
Put the pork in a large food bag with the marinade, seal it and turn to coat the meat. Leave in the fridge for 8 to 24 hours, turning it now and then.

Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Line a roasting tin with banana leaves or foil, tip in the pork and its marinade and wrap it tightly so no steam escapes. If using banana leaves, an outer layer of foil helps seal it.
Roast for 4 hours. Open the parcel carefully: the pork should shred easily with a fork.
Serve over rice, or shred it and serve in taco shells or tortillas.

recipes.title: Machacado con huevo
recipes.description: Shredded dried beef stirred through softly scrambled eggs, a northern Mexican breakfast served with warm tortillas, refried beans, cheese and salsa.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 10 ea. 8-inch soft taco-size flour tortillas, warmed
2 cups (8 ounces) shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack Cheese

steps: Melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Add the eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often, until they just begin to set.
Stir in the shredded beef and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the eggs are cooked and the beef is hot through.
Serve with the warm tortillas, refried beans, cheese and salsa.

recipes.title: Falafel
recipes.description: Crisp little balls of soaked chickpeas blitzed with garlic, onion, parsley and warm spices, fried golden and served with pitta.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 cloves of garlic, peeled and sliced
½ cup vegetable oil (sunflower or corn oil) for frying

steps: The night before, put the chickpeas in a bowl and cover with plenty of water, at least a few centimetres above them, as they swell. Drain, rinse and dry them before using.
Purée the chickpeas in a food processor or blender, then add everything else except the oil and blend until well mixed.
Shape the mixture into balls, using about a tablespoon for each.
Heat the oil in a medium frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the balls and fry until browned all over.
Serve with pitta.

recipes.title: Fattoush
recipes.description: A crunchy Lebanese salad of lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, herbs and toasted pitta, tossed in a sharp lemon and sumac dressing.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 1 head romaine lettuce, torn into bite-size pieces
¼ cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
4 pita rounds, toasted and torn into pieces

steps: Stir the water and cornflour together in a small saucepan over a medium-high heat until thickened.
Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, garlic, sumac, salt and pepper.
Chill the dressing until you're ready to use it.
In a large bowl, toss together the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, spring onions, parsley, mint, green pepper, purslane and rocket.
Toss with the dressing and serve with the toasted pitta.

recipes.title: Ghormeh sabzi
recipes.description: A slow-cooked Persian stew of beef or lamb, red kidney beans, a mass of green herbs and sour dried limes, served with saffron rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 800 g beef or lamb which has some fat (such as the meat for boiled beef)
1 can (about 400 g) fried ghormeh sabzi herbs

steps: Boil the red kidney beans for 1 hour, then drain.
Trim any excess fat from the meat and cut it into smaller pieces.
Heat the oil in a big pan with a lid. Add the onions and fry over a high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in the meat and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes.
Turn the heat down as low as it goes. The meat will release plenty of juice, which flavours the stew.
Stir in the parsley, spinach, coriander and ghormeh sabzi herbs.
Stir in about 500 ml of boiling water, or enough to give a good consistency.
Stir in the cooked beans and simmer over a low heat for 30 minutes to 3 hours; the longer the better.
Soak the dried limes in hot water for 15 minutes, then pierce each one with a fork.
Add the dried limes, turmeric, pepper and salt to the stew and simmer for another 30 minutes to 1 hour.
If you like, let the stew cool and keep it in the fridge: it tastes better over the next two days.
Steam the rice.
Grind the saffron with the sugar in a mortar, then add about a tablespoon of boiling water. Toss some of the cooked rice with the saffron water to colour it.
Serve the stew hot in its own bowl, with the plain rice in a separate bowl topped with the saffron rice.

recipes.title: Pitta bread
recipes.description: Soft, puffy flatbreads made from a simple yeasted dough of durum wheat flour, for filling with salad, falafel or grilled meat.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: plus a little for your hands and the work surface

ingredient_lines.original_text: 500 ml (2 cups or 17 fl oz) durum wheat flour

steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water in a large bowl. Add the salt, oil and flour, mix, then knead into a smooth dough. It is sticky, so oil your hands and the work surface rather than adding more flour.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough to rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about an hour.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and shape each into a ball.
Roll each ball into a flat round about 15 cm across.
Lay the rounds on a baking tray, cover with a cloth and leave in a warm place to rise for about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 225°C (205°C fan).
Bake for about 12 minutes, until puffed and lightly coloured.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.description: Eggs gently cooked in a pan of soft onion, tomatoes and peppers with warm spices, ready to be scooped up with bread.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Cayenne pepper, paprika, and turmeric to taste
Cayenne pepper, paprika, and turmeric to taste
Cayenne pepper, paprika, and turmeric to taste

steps: Peel and chop the onion and fry it in the oil until translucent.
Chop the tomatoes and pepper and add them to the onion in the pan.
Add the basil and spices. Cover and cook over a low heat until the tomatoes are cooked through, about 25 minutes.
With a wooden spoon, make two hollows in the tomato mixture.
Crack an egg into each hollow. Cover and cook until the eggs are set, about 5 minutes more.
Serve with bread.

recipes.title: Gambas al ajillo
recipes.description: Prawns sizzled in olive oil with plenty of garlic, sherry, lemon and sweet paprika, the Spanish tapas bar favourite.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 4–6 large cloves of garlic, finely minced
2–3 oz dry sherry (you may substitute cognac instead)

steps: Warm the olive oil in a sauté pan or other heavy frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for about a minute, until it starts to colour. Take care not to let it burn.
Turn the heat up to high and add the prawns, lemon juice, sherry and paprika. Stir well, then cook, stirring briskly, for about 3 minutes, until the prawns turn pink and curl.
Take the pan off the heat and tip the prawns, oil and sauce onto a warm plate, or serve straight from the pan.
Season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper and scatter over the parsley.

recipes.title: Gazpacho
recipes.description: A chilled Andalusian soup of blended tomatoes, peppers, cucumber, garlic and olive oil, served with little bowls of chopped vegetables and croutons.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: white, 2 to 3 days old; leave it out for a thinner soup
lines.original_text: 2 oz (50 g) 2–3 day-old white bread (optional—leave out for a thinner soup)
1 lb (450 g) tomatoes, skinned and quartered
½ lb (225 g) green bell peppers, seeded and trimmed
½ cucumber, peeled and cut in chunks
1 tbsp white or red wine vinegar
½ green bell pepper, diced fine

steps: If using the bread for the soup, tear it up and soak it in water for 30 minutes, then squeeze it dry.

Put the soaked bread, tomatoes, green pepper, cucumber, garlic, onion, vinegar, olive oil, chilli, coriander and iced water in a blender and blend until roughly chopped. The soup should keep some texture and small pieces of vegetable, so don't blend it too finely.
Pour the soup into a large bowl with some ice cubes and season to taste with salt and pepper. Keep it in the fridge until it is well chilled.
For the garnish, dice the bread and fry it in a little olive oil in a frying pan until golden.
Finely chop the tomato, green pepper and cucumber for the garnish, and put each garnish in its own small bowl.
Serve the gazpacho chilled, and let everyone add their own garnishes at the table.

recipes.title: Pad thai
recipes.description: Stir-fried rice noodles with prawns, egg and beansprouts in a sweet, sour and salty tamarind and fish sauce dressing, finished with peanuts and lime.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or rice vinegar, plus more to taste
ingredient_lines.original_text: 3+ tablespoons (50 ml) white vinegar (or rice vinegar)
¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon (75 ml) tamarind juice
¼ cup and 1 tablespoon (75 ml) palm sugar (or granulated sugar)
2 tablespoons (30 ml) dried red chili pepper flakes (or to taste)

ingredient_lines.note: or tofu, chicken, squid or beef, or a mix
ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ pound (225 g) of shrimp, tofu, chicken, squid, or beef (or a combination thereof)
Assorted vegetables (e.g., shredded carrots, white onions, red or green peppers)
Assorted vegetables (e.g., shredded carrots, white onions, red or green peppers)
Assorted vegetables (e.g., shredded carrots, white onions, red or green peppers)
¾ cup (175 ml) chopped unroasted peanuts

steps: Soak the noodles in warm water for about 20 minutes, then drain. Or pour boiling water over them, leave for 7 minutes and drain.
Mix the fish sauce, vinegar, palm sugar and tamarind juice together in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the garlic and chilli flakes for a minute until the garlic browns.
Add the prawns (or whichever protein you are using) and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until browned.
Add the carrot, onion and pepper and stir-fry until tender.
Add the noodles, crack the eggs over them, let them set a little and then toss everything together.
Pour in the fish sauce mixture, toss well and turn the heat down to medium.
Add the spring onions and beansprouts and stir-fry for 2 minutes more.
Serve on a large plate or in bowls, scattered with the chopped peanuts, and with coriander and lime wedges if you like.

recipes.title: Tom kha kai
recipes.description: A fragrant Thai chicken soup simmered in coconut milk and stock with lemongrass, galangal and bird's eye chillies, sharpened with lime juice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: stalks, cut into 3 cm pieces or split lengthways
ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 stalks lemongrass, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) pieces or split lengthwise
2 x 1-inch (5 x 2.5 cm) cube galangal, sliced thin
3–4 mini Thai bird chilies, finely chopped

steps: Bring the stock and coconut milk to the boil in a large pan.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, most of the chillies, the sugar and the pepper.
Add the onion, tomato, chicken and mushrooms.
Keep it at a rolling boil for 4 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lime juice and soy sauce.
Serve scattered with the coriander and the rest of the chillies.

recipes.title: Menemen
recipes.description: Turkish eggs softly scrambled into onions, green peppers and tomatoes cooked down in olive oil, with parsley and a little paprika.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water, then peel, deseed and dice them. Or simply grate them on a box grater or blitz them in a food processor.
Dice the onions and peppers and fry them gently in the olive oil in a frying pan until soft.
Stir in the oregano and paprika, if using.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Beat the eggs, pour them over the vegetables and stir until just cooked.
Serve with Turkish bread, or a crisp baguette.

recipes.title: Canh chua
recipes.description: A Vietnamese sweet and sour fish soup with pineapple and sour bamboo shoots, seasoned with fish sauce and finished with coriander and spring onion.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: whole, or another firm white fish
lines.original_text: 1 whole catfish or other firm white fish

lines.note: green parts kept for the garnish, white parts crushed
lines.original_text: 2 scallions, green part reserved for garnish and white part crushed
¼ fresh pineapple, core removed, cut lengthwise and sliced

lines.note: the green parts kept from the marinade, chopped

steps: Marinate the fish for 15 minutes with the crushed white parts of the spring onions, black pepper, salt and fish sauce.
Bring the water to the boil in a large pan. Add the sour bamboo shoots and pineapple and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the marinated fish and boil for 10 minutes in all. While it cooks, stir in the fish sauce and salt for the soup.
Serve garnished with the coriander and the chopped green parts of the spring onions.

recipes.title: Summer rolls
recipes.description: Soft Vietnamese rice paper rolls filled with prawns, pork, rice vermicelli, crisp vegetables and fresh herbs, made with no cooking at all.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 50 g cooked pork or chicken meat
4 leaves of leafy lettuce (e.g. romaine/cos, mignonette, etc.)
2 leaves of Chinese cabbage, halved lengthways
Fresh herbs, to taste (e.g. coriander, basil, mint)
Fresh herbs, to taste (e.g. coriander, basil, mint)
Fresh herbs, to taste (e.g. coriander, basil, mint)

steps: Dip a rice paper wrapper into the warm water and lift it out as soon as it is wet all over; it only needs a few seconds.
Lay the wrapper flat on a board or plate.
Pile a quarter of the prawns, pork, vermicelli, cucumber, lettuce, cabbage and herbs neatly near one edge, with the cucumber fingers running parallel to the edge.
Fold that edge of the wrapper over the filling and roll it over once.
Fold in the sides of the wrapper to close the ends.
Roll the rest of the way to enclose the filling completely.
Leave for 5 minutes to dry a little before eating. Repeat with the rest of the wrappers and filling.
